title: Introduction of the Heritage program; music is music
summary: The host introduces Armstrong and guests Benny Benack and Frederick Dorian. Armstrong says a note is a note in any language.

blocks.x: Great with life itself, and with our heritage. In this series of heritage programs, we are privileged to meet Mr. Louis Armstrong, the internationally known New Orleans jazz trumpeter and band leader. In this fourth program, Mr. Armstrong and his guests, Mr. Benny Benack, jazz trumpeter, band leader, and assistant director of the University of Pittsburgh Band, and Dr. Frederick Dorian, musicologist at Carnegie Institute of Technology and program annotator for the Pittsburgh Symphony, will discuss jazz is just good music.

A lot of people start breaking music down, and they say, this is good music, and that's bad, whether it's symphony or jazz. And actually, I think music is music, and I think there's a purpose for music. Maybe that's the thing. Maybe we shouldn't say it's good technically, or it's good this way, or structurally. Maybe there's a feeling we should get out of music. What do you think about it? You say, a lot of people that go in and do all that, they don't know anything about music. You understand? They try to find out trends, that's something. But a man that traveled all over the world, like I did, I find out that a note's a note in any language. You hit that note, you get your applause.
